Area.evidence_source: ['018_seeking_help_outside_the_network'] Finally, informants talked about the difficulty of knowing when, where, and how to seek help outside the social network. Even informants who worked in the health sector or had experience of using mental health services themselves complained of lack of knowledge of available avenues. In some cases, lack of confidence and a fear of not being taken seriously may have deterred both the deceased and significant others from approaching professional agencies: ['018_seeking_help_outside_the_network'] Mother: "Probably he thought, oh, they won't believe me anyway, 'cos that was drummed into his head when he was being abused . . . If you're not very good at explaining, which I feel sometimes I'm not, I'm not very good with big words and whatever, you just can't get over how you feel." ['018_seeking_help_outside_the_network'] Others made it clear that their family's coping style did not include seeking professional help: ['018_seeking_help_outside_the_network'] Mother: "We're basically copers, my family . . . Stiff upper lip, don't make a big deal of it, don't let's have a drama . . . I haven't been near my GP since all this happened." ['018_seeking_help_outside_the_network'] Previous bad experiences of mental healthcare, the negative public image of local services, and the desire to protect the loved one from involuntary incarceration were all cited as disincentives to seeking medical advice: ['018_seeking_help_outside_the_network'] Mother: "He was very, very scared of being sectioned . . . because some of the people he knew had been sectioned . . . That's why [friend] didn't call the police . . . because she knew he was frightened." ['018_seeking_help_outside_the_network'] Another informant spoke poignantly of her confidence in her own ability to manage the situation and her belief in the healing power of love: ['018_seeking_help_outside_the_network'] Partner: "I know I'm naive and ridiculous, but I believed . . . that my love and the children's ['page/5/Text/4'] unconditional love . . . would be enough. Ultimately I thought we would heal him." ['page/5/Text/5'] Some informants admitted that, misjudging the urgency of the situation and unsure of the best approach to take, they had simply put off taking any action at all.
